title: I made a party of three ARPG using Godot and AI workflows!
author: NIGHTrock16
selftext:
I've been working on **Below the Keep**, a dungeon-crawling ARPG where you control a party of three heroes. You swap between them mid-fight, chain their skills together, and bring loot back to camp to upgrade your gear. The weapon each hero holds decides their skills, so any hero can play any class. It's a hobby project I started to learn how far I could get by building a full game with AI.

**How AI was used**

* **Code: Claude Code.** Almost all of the code was written by Claude in Godot 4 (GDScript). I make the design calls, playtest and review, and Claude builds and tests. I run several Claude sessions in parallel, each in its own git worktree for one feature (bosses, sound, balance, effects), with an automated test suite of about 4,000 tests that runs before anything merges into main. Keeping handoff notes and a decisions log was the biggest thing that made it work over weeks of sessions.
* **3D models: Meshy.** The characters, enemies, bosses and weapons started as Meshy generations. Claude then cleaned them up in Blender through the Blender MCP: rigging, fixing normals, re-baking textures and adjusting animations. Raw Meshy output needed a lot of work before it looked right in game.
* **Sound and music: ElevenLabs** made the sound effects and music the stock library didn't cover. Most everyday sounds come from a regular sound pack, because I wanted short, simple sounds for things you hear constantly.
* **Art: ChatGPT** made the title-screen painting, which Claude cut into animated layers.
* **Balance: a simulation Claude wrote.** It runs the party, gear and Forge upgrades floor by floor, so we can tune the numbers before playing them.

**What was hard:** models looked fine in a viewer but broke in game (textures that showed seams from a distance, animations that popped between clips). Getting combat to feel good also took far more rounds of playtesting than writing the systems did.

**The playtest is live now** (free, Windows). I'm looking for honest feedback on:

* How the combat feels and whether swapping heroes is fun
* Difficulty and pacing on the first few floors
* Bugs, crashes and performance on your hardware

Join the Discord and grab the Playtester role to get the download: [https://discord.gg/aN7GVK7u7C](https://discord.gg/aN7GVK7u7C)

You can also visit the website: [belowthekeep.com](http://belowthekeep.com)

Happy to answer questions about the workflow, what worked, and what didn't.
